title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks with same price increase saw sales 10% and 10% below baseline (10 and 7 vs 7.8); consistent downward pressure; noise-adjusted effect of promotions is weak (x1.16), suggesting limited demand elasticity.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.8. The target week has no event or promotion, but a 2.3% price increase to $9.03. Recent weeks show a 2.3% price increase on 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05, both with sales of 10 and 7 units—below baseline (7.8), suggesting a price sensitivity. The noise-adjusted effect of past promotions (x1.16) is weak, and the uplift model sees no signal. The price increase likely reduces demand. Given the baseline’s high noise (64%) and limited evidence, shrink toward 1.0. No seasonal or event driver. The price increase is the only driver.

It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
